name: Pride and Prejudice
kicker: Jane Austen’s 1813 novel of manners · A classic enemies-to-lovers romance
briefing: Jane Austen’s _Pride and Prejudice_ opens with Mrs. Bennet desperate to marry off her five daughters, and sharp-tongued Elizabeth Bennet convinced that the rich, standoffish Mr. Darcy is simply too proud to like anyone. Over balls, letters, and a disastrous marriage proposal, the two slowly discover how wrong their first impressions were. More than two hundred years later, it is still one of the most-loved love stories in English.

qb.tip: All 8 are the same answer line with no namesake confusion; the Lydia/Wickham elopement and Charlotte Lucas marrying Mr. Collins are the two most common supporting clues.

sample.note: the 8 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: This novel’s Lady Catherine de Bourgh [“boorg”] had long hoped her nephew would marry her own daughter, Anne, instead of this novel’s heroine. While visiting his aunt at Rosings Park, that nephew makes a first marriage proposal that is angrily refused, partly over his role in separating a friend from the heroine’s older sister.
tossups.r: A letter from that nephew later reveals that a charming militia officer had tried to elope with his young sister for her fortune. For 10 points, name this novel in which Fitzwilliam Darcy eventually marries Elizabeth Bennet, by Jane Austen.

tossups.p: Jane Austen’s working title for this novel, before she revised it years later, was _First Impressions_. At an assembly ball early in this novel, one guest refuses to dance with anyone outside his own party and is overheard calling the heroine “not handsome enough to tempt” him.
tossups.r: Charlotte Lucas marries the pompous clergyman Mr. Collins after her friend turns down his proposal in this novel. For 10 points, name this novel in which the Bennet sisters search for husbands, by Jane Austen.

tossups.p: This novel has been called a comedy of manners that pokes fun at the courtship rituals of the British landed gentry. Because the Bennet family in this novel has no sons, a distant cousin stands to inherit their estate at Longbourn under an entail.
tossups.r: Mr. Bingley rents the nearby estate of Netherfield Park in this novel, setting off a chain of misunderstandings. For 10 points, name this novel that begins with a line about a single man in possession of a good fortune, by Jane Austen.

tossups.p: A militia officer in this novel first turns the heroine against a rich acquaintance by falsely claiming that man cheated him out of an inheritance. That same officer’s scheme to secretly marry the rich man’s young sister is exposed in a long letter in this novel.
tossups.r: The heroine later tours the estate of Pemberley with her aunt and uncle, the Gardiners, and is impressed by how kindly its owner treats his servants. For 10 points, name this novel in which Elizabeth Bennet eventually marries Mr. Darcy, by Jane Austen.

tossups.p: This novel was published anonymously in 1813, credited on its title page only to “the Author of _Sense and Sensibility_.” Its author revised it from a draft she had written in her twenties at her family’s home in Hampshire, England.
tossups.r: That author had earlier called this novel _First Impressions_ before settling on a title that names two character flaws. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel about Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth Bennet.

tossups.p: This novel’s hero has the first name Fitzwilliam, and his judgmental aunt is Lady Catherine de Bourgh of Rosings Park. That aunt had wanted her nephew to marry her own daughter instead of this novel’s heroine.
tossups.r: Late in this novel, Lady Catherine visits the heroine’s home at Longbourn to warn her away from marrying Darcy, without success. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel in which Elizabeth Bennet accepts Darcy’s second proposal.

tossups.p: A 2009 mash-up novel adds a zombie apocalypse to this novel’s plot while keeping most of its original sentences. At an assembly ball in the real version of this novel, the heroine overhears a rich guest describe her as “not handsome enough to tempt” him.
tossups.r: The heroine’s sister Jane falls for Mr. Bingley, while her youngest sister Lydia runs off with the dishonorable George Wickham in this novel. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel, not the zombie parody of the same name.

tossups.p: Because the family at the center of this novel has five daughters and no sons, their home at Longbourn is entailed to a distant male cousin. That cousin proposes marriage to the novel’s heroine before marrying her friend Charlotte Lucas instead.
tossups.r: The hero of this novel secretly pays off George Wickham to marry the heroine’s disgraced youngest sister. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel in which Mr. Darcy marries Elizabeth Bennet.

tossups.p: This novel is often read as a comedy of manners about the marriage market of the British landed gentry. Its hero’s first marriage proposal, delivered while he is visiting his aunt’s estate of Rosings Park, is rejected by its heroine as arrogant.
tossups.r: The heroine later visits Pemberley with her aunt and uncle the Gardiners and begins to see her future husband differently. For 10 points, name this novel in which Elizabeth Bennet eventually accepts Mr. Darcy’s second proposal, by Jane Austen.

tossups.p: Jane Austen revised this novel from a draft written in her twenties at her family’s Hampshire home before publishing it anonymously in 1813. Early in this novel, a militia officer falsely claims that the hero cheated him out of an inheritance from the hero’s late father.
tossups.r: That lie turns the heroine against the hero until his later letter exposes the officer’s true, dishonorable character. For 10 points, name this novel in which Charlotte Lucas marries Mr. Collins, by Jane Austen.

tossups.p: This novel’s Lady Catherine de Bourgh once hoped her own daughter, the sickly Anne, would marry Darcy instead of this novel’s heroine. A 2009 parody novel keeps most of this novel’s sentences but adds a zombie outbreak to its plot.
tossups.r: At an early ball in the real novel, the heroine overhears Darcy call her “not handsome enough to tempt” him. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel in which that same Darcy eventually marries Elizabeth Bennet.

tossups.p: This novel, whose hero’s full first name is Fitzwilliam, was published anonymously in 1813. That hero’s second marriage proposal succeeds only after the heroine sees how kindly he treats his servants and tenants at his estate, Pemberley.
tossups.r: Earlier in this novel, that same hero’s first proposal, made while he is visiting his aunt at Rosings Park, is furiously rejected. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel about Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth Bennet.

tossups.p: Jane Austen originally titled this novel _First Impressions_ before revising and renaming it. Because the family at this novel’s center has no sons, their estate at Longbourn is entailed to their cousin Mr. Collins, a clergyman.
tossups.r: Late in this novel, the hero’s aunt Lady Catherine de Bourgh visits Longbourn to try to talk the heroine out of marrying her nephew. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel in which Elizabeth Bennet marries Mr. Darcy.

tossups.p: This novel is often described as a comedy of manners satirizing how the British landed gentry arranged marriages. A long letter in this novel reveals that a militia officer once tried to secretly marry the hero’s young sister, Georgiana, purely for her fortune.
tossups.r: The hero of this novel later pays that same officer, George Wickham, to marry the heroine’s disgraced sister Lydia. For 10 points, name this novel that begins with a line about a single man in possession of a good fortune, by Jane Austen.

tossups.p: Jane Austen revised this novel from a draft she wrote in her twenties at her family’s home in Hampshire. A 2009 parody of this novel keeps most of Austen’s original sentences while adding zombies to the plot.
tossups.r: The real version of this novel is set mainly at the estates of Longbourn, Netherfield, and Pemberley. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel in which Elizabeth Bennet marries Mr. Darcy.

trap.title: Original, or zombie parody?
trap.body: A 2009 mash-up novel, _Pride and Prejudice and Zombies_, reuses most of Austen’s own sentences but adds a zombie outbreak. Quiz bowl wants only the original 1813 novel. Clues about Elinor and Marianne belong to _Sense and Sensibility_; clues about Emma Woodhouse belong to _Emma_ — both are separate Austen answer lines.
trap.fix: If a clue mentions zombies, rotting corpses, or Seth Grahame-Smith, that is the parody, not this answer. If it names a different Austen heroine (Elinor, Marianne, Emma, Anne Elliot, Catherine Morland, Fanny Price), it is a different novel.
